EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The single most critical development of the past 24 hours is Iran's declaration of a shift to a "fully offensive" policy, issuing a "deadline of several weeks" for the United States to implement their Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). Tehran warns it will not tolerate an indefinite American naval blockade and is prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the region if diplomacy fails. This signifies a heightened risk of direct confrontation or significant regional destabilization.

IRAN
A senior Iranian official informed Reuters that Tehran has decided to shift from a defensive posture to a "fully offensive" policy, setting a "deadline of several weeks" for the United States to fully implement their MOU. Iran warns it will not tolerate an indefinite US naval blockade and is prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the region if diplomacy fails. This deadline is to be conveyed to the US and regional states via mediators. The IRGC Spokesman, Brigadier General Mohebi, denied Trump's claims of secret talks with the IRGC, dismissing them as "fantasies born of delusion and nightmares stemming from defeat and desperation in the war." He stated that the IRGC acts on the battlefield, while diplomatic issues fall to other government sectors, which are not currently engaged in talks with the US due to past violations. General Jovani, a political aide to the IRGC Commander, stated that Iran's armed forces would adopt a "transformative-offensive approach." The IRGC has also stated that the Strait of Hormuz will only reopen when the US honors its commitments under the Islamabad MoU. Marine Traffic reports a 19.5% decrease in traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with daily crossings plummeting from 19 on August 11 to just 3 on August 16. The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman clarified that the Islamabad MoU does not stipulate a 60-day deadline and that no talks have begun due to Washington's violations, although Al Arabiya reported an agreement to extend the 60-day ceasefire. Economically, Middle East Eye reported that the war against Iran has plunged the Middle East aviation industry into crisis, projecting potential net losses of $4.3 billion for airlines. The Iranian Minister of Oil stated that attacks on four refineries reduced South Pars production by one third, making full reconstruction with internal means impossible for 1.5 to 2 years, and predicted a gas shortage in the cold season. Oil prices remained stable at $88.55 per barrel for Brent crude. Internally, President Pazeshkian announced plans to end internet censorship, a process expected to take time. The Tehran prosecutor announced intensified crackdowns on hijab and virtual space violations, establishing a special "morality security prosecutor's office."

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted airstrikes in al-Mansouri and Nabatieh in southern Lebanon, with continuous strikes also reported in the Ali Taher hills. In Gaza, the IDF responded with strikes in the northern Gaza Strip after a Hamas bomb exploded on the Israeli side of the "Yellow Line" and militants opened fire, reporting no Israeli casualties. Prime Minister Netanyahu met with Jared Kushner and Nikolai Mladenov, CEO of the Peace Council, to discuss the Gaza plan. They agreed that no reconstruction in Gaza would begin until Hamas is fully disarmed, including both heavy and light weapons, under US supervision. Israel will retain its freedom of action, including targeted strikes, and will not withdraw from the Yellow Line where security requires it. A second working group was established to focus on sanitation and clean water in Gaza. Netanyahu reportedly criticized Kushner for meeting with Hamas leaders. On the home front, the local council of Shlomi, near the Lebanese border, is conducting shooting training for residents with firearm licenses, including drills for terrorist infiltration, reflecting a lack of trust in the ceasefire. Justice Minister Ben-Gvir demanded administrative detention powers and the transfer of Border Police responsibility in the West Bank from the IDF to the Israel Police. Likud primaries are underway, with a turnout of 26.44% (over 37,000 voters) by midday, a 1.4% increase from 2022. Early polls suggest a tie between Gantz and Netanyahu with 23 Knesset seats each. Civilian incidents include a one-year-old infant critically injured after falling from a playground in Hadera, two children (ages 4 and 9) stabbed in Beit Shemesh (the 9-year-old in critical condition), and another 4-year-old child killed by a vehicle in Beit Shemesh.

GAZA & WEST BANK
A Hamas bomb exploded overnight on the Israeli side of the "Yellow Line" in the northern Gaza Strip, followed by gunfire from militants. The IDF responded with retaliatory strikes in the area, reporting no Israeli casualties. Israeli forces, accompanied by bulldozers, raided the Palestinian village of Qalandia, north of Al-Quds, raising concerns about demolitions. In the West Bank, an individual was arrested in Nablus (Shchem) for allegedly planning an immediate attack against soldiers or civilians, with authorities seizing 150,000 NIS, rifles, and incitement materials. A 36-year-old resident of Qalandia camp was arrested for attempting to dig a tunnel near the separation barrier, with digging tools found at the site. The UN reports a sharp rise in settler violence against Palestinians, with nearly 3,000 attacks recorded since January 2025. The Palestinian village of Qusra remains under a nine-day siege by settlers, hindering aid access. On the diplomatic front, Israel and the Peace Council agreed that Gaza reconstruction is contingent on Hamas's full disarmament under US supervision. Hamas welcomed President Trump's call for a ceasefire from Israel and urged him to pressure the Israeli government to implement Phase 2 of the proposed Gaza peace plan. Jared Kushner met with Hamas leaders in Egypt to advance the disarmament aspect of the Gaza plan.

LEBANON
Israeli forces conducted two new attacks on the town of al-Mansouri and also targeted Nabatieh in southern Lebanon. Reports also indicate continuous Israeli strikes in the Ali Taher hills in the south. The Amal Movement condemned the Israeli attacks as "massacres of ordinary civilians" and stated that direct negotiations with Israel are "unjustified" given the ongoing violence. Lebanese President Aoun asserted that relations with Iran must be based on mutual respect, without internal interference, and should be state-to-state. The attacks in southern Lebanon have previously led to hundreds of families fleeing and roads to the north being blocked, as reported by Al Jazeera.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Two drones, reportedly launched from within Iran, targeted the private office of Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the residence of the Director of the Protection Agency in Erbil, northern Iraq. No casualties were reported. Masrour Barzani condemned these "brazen and unacceptable aggressions" as a dangerous escalation. Iraqi Kurdish President Nechirvan Barzani called on the Baghdad government to uphold its constitutional responsibilities for Iraq's security. A US surveillance balloon was again spotted in the skies over Erbil Province. The Iraqi Prime Minister, Ali Falih al-Zaidi, warned that Iraq is among the countries most vulnerable to any closure of the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting the significant economic and energy consequences. Plans to export Iraqi oil via a pipeline through Syria are estimated to take four years and cost at least $15 billion. Internal security incidents in Iraq include the kidnapping of Abu Al-Jood, a PMF intelligence unit leader, in Baghdad, which sparked protests in Al-Fadhliya (Nasiriyah). A mine explosion in Basra resulted in one fatality. In Maysan province, three police officers were injured during clashes with protesters demonstrating over services, leading government forces to raid the area. The Iraqi Communications and Media Commission issued sanctions against Al-Fallujah TV and banned two commentators from appearing on media.

GULF STATES
Yemeni Houthi forces claimed to have launched several ballistic missiles at a Saudi military landing ship and four escort boats off the coast of Al Mokha in the Red Sea. They reported the vessel was set completely ablaze, with several boats sinking and others catching fire. Subsequently, Marine Traffic reported a 6.7% increase in crossings through Bab al-Mandab, but Saudi Arabia has reportedly halted its oil shipments through the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait due to heightened insecurity. Sultan Haitham bin Tariq of Oman met with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed in Abu Dhabi, where they discussed common interests and regional security and stability. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman confirmed ongoing intensive negotiations with Oman to establish a safe shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. However, President Trump threatened to "bomb the sh*t out of" Oman if it interferes. The Wall Street Journal reported that Kuwait, a more vulnerable Gulf state, is concerned about Iran's alleged plans for offensive military actions. Saudi Arabia is reportedly removing the name "Palestine" and the slogan "Muslims will never give up Jerusalem" from its school textbooks. President Trump expressed satisfaction that Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan "finally signed the Mecca defense agreement," calling it a "big, bold, and important first step" for regional defense cooperation.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iran's Shift to Offensive Policy:** A senior Iranian official announced a decision to adopt a "fully offensive" policy and set a "deadline of several weeks" for the US to implement their MOU, threatening regional escalation, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz, if diplomacy fails.
2.  **Strait of Hormuz Gridlock:** The IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz will only reopen upon US adherence to Islamabad MoU commitments. Marine Traffic reported a 19.5% reduction in crossings through the Strait, with daily transits falling from 19 to 3.
3.  **Houthi Red Sea Attack:** Yemeni Houthi forces claimed a ballistic missile attack on a Saudi military landing ship and four escort boats off Al Mokha, Red Sea, causing the vessel to ignite and other boats to sink or burn. Saudi Arabia reportedly halted oil shipments through Bab al-Mandab due to this insecurity.
4.  **Gaza Reconstruction Conditions:** Israeli PM Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed that Gaza reconstruction requires full Hamas disarmament (heavy and light weapons) under US supervision, with Israel retaining freedom of action for targeted strikes.
5.  **Iranian Drone Attacks in Erbil:** Two drones, reportedly launched from inside Iran, targeted the private office of Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the residence of the Protection Agency Director in Erbil, Iraq.
6.  **Trump's Contradictory Iran Stance:** President Trump stated "no rush" for Iran talks, called for Iran to "raise a white flag," claimed a "secret channel with the IRGC," but also threatened to "bomb the sh*t out of" Oman if it interferes in Hormuz. Former US Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene claimed discussions about using nuclear weapons against Iran are occurring within the Trump administration.
7.  **Israeli Strikes in Southern Lebanon:** Israeli forces conducted airstrikes in al-Mansouri and Nabatieh, and continuously in the Ali Taher hills, in southern Lebanon.
8.  **Hamas Ceasefire Violation in Gaza:** A Hamas bomb exploded on the Israeli side of the "Yellow Line" in the northern Gaza Strip, accompanied by militant gunfire, prompting retaliatory IDF strikes.
9.  **Mecca Defense Agreement:** Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan reportedly signed a "Mecca defense agreement" for regional cooperation, hailed by Trump as a significant step for self-defense.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are HIGH. Iran's explicit declaration of an "offensive policy" with a stated deadline for US compliance on the MoU, coupled with its refusal to tolerate an indefinite naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, signals an imminent and deliberate move toward heightened confrontation. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab strait (marked by Houthi attacks on Saudi vessels), southern Lebanon (Israeli airstrikes), and northern Gaza (Hamas ceasefire violations and Israeli retaliation). The Iranian drone attacks in Iraqi Kurdistan further underscore regional instability. Military postures are shifting, with Iran reportedly accelerating missile and drone production and reorganizing its military command in preparation for prolonged conflict. The US order to significantly reduce military exercises with South Korea could indicate a strategic reallocation of resources or a diplomatic overture. Red lines include Iran's deadline regarding the MoU, the US's unequivocal stance against Iranian nuclear weapons, and Israel's demands for full Hamas disarmament as a prerequisite for Gaza reconstruction, alongside its insistence on maintaining freedom of action.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture on Iran remains contradictory: President Trump claimed "no rush" for talks and urged Iran to "raise a white flag," while also asserting a "secret channel with the IRGC," a claim vehemently denied by Tehran. He threatened to "bomb the sh*t out of" Oman if it interferes in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also ordered a significant reduction of joint US-South Korea military exercises. Gulf states are navigating the heightened tensions; Saudi Arabia has halted oil shipments through Bab al-Mandab following Houthi attacks, and Oman's Sultan met with the UAE President to discuss regional stability. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have reportedly signed a "Mecca defense agreement." Iraq's Prime Minister warned of severe consequences for his country if Hormuz closes, and Iraqi Kurdish President Nechirvan Barzani condemned drone attacks on Erbil while also offering to mediate US-Iran talks. Hamas welcomed Trump's calls for an Israeli ceasefire and urged him to pressure Israel to implement the next phase of the Gaza peace plan. The Amal Movement in Lebanon condemned Israeli strikes and deemed talks with Israel "unjustified." South Korea, despite the reduction in US drills, expressed hope for "meaningful talks" with the US and North Korea.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the intelligence. President Trump's assertion of a "secret channel with the IRGC" was directly and strongly refuted by the IRGC Spokesman, who characterized it as "fantasies." The status and specific deadlines of the "Islamabad MoU" are highly ambiguous, with Al Arabiya reporting an extension, but the Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman denying a 60-day deadline and stating no talks have commenced due to US violations, while Israeli channels indicate the 60-day period expires today. Trump's claims regarding Iran's military and economic collapse (e.g., 159 ships sunk, no airplanes, 350% inflation) appear to be significant exaggerations or propaganda. The claim by former US Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene about discussions within the Trump administration regarding the use of nuclear weapons against Iran is a serious, unverified claim from a controversial source. Trump's statement that "Hamas agreed to lay down arms" is contradicted by Hamas's recent actions (bomb and gunfire in Gaza) and Netanyahu's statements on Hamas violations. There is no official confirmation from Saudi Arabia regarding the Houthi attack on their military vessel. Key reporting gaps include the specific terms of the "Islamabad MoU" and the "Mecca defense agreement," the exact identity of the "anti-Hamas militia" in Gaza, and detailed damage assessments from Israeli strikes in Lebanon. Propaganda is evident in various statements, including Trump's rhetoric, the IRGC's strong denials, Iranian officials emphasizing victory, and Netanyahu's Likud campaign messaging.
